title: Skip It: Take Control of Your Cache!
problem: Explicit cache management mechanisms are critical for correctness and performance but incur significant performance penalties. These mechanisms are implemented in proprietary, undocumented hardware, limiting research into optimizations and novel designs.
motivation: User-controlled cache management is essential for modern system performance, yet existing solutions have high overhead and limited transparency for experimentation.
method: The paper adds extensions to a CPU that let programs control when cached data is written back to main memory (the slower, larger memory storage). It introduces "Skip It," a filter that detects and blocks redundant writebacks—situations where the same data is being unnecessarily written multiple times. The design was implemented on BOOM, an open-source out-of-order RISC-V processor, and achieved approximately 100-cycle latency for these operations.
key_novelty: Skip It filters out redundant cache writebacks, substantially reducing memory transfer overhead.
contributions: Microarchitectural extensions for two types of user-controlled cache writebacks to main memory
Skip It mechanism to substantially reduce redundant writebacks
Implementation on open-source BOOM out-of-order RISC-V CPU achieving ~100 cycle performance
Competitive performance validation against commercial server-class platforms and software techniques

metrics.speedup: ~100 cycles for cache writebacks, comparable to commercial server platforms
metrics.other: performs as well as or better than state-of-the-art software optimization techniques

baselines: state-of-the-art software techniques for avoiding unnecessary writebacks
limitations: Specific workload performance impact, power consumption analysis, and multi-core scalability not discussed.
